bull_bear.body: The company has a robust working capital position with a sanctioned limit of Rs 745 Cr and an unutilized limit of Rs 337 Cr.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Cash flow constraints, internal organizational changes, and competition in the infrastructure and real estate sectors
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's focus on mid-market residential projects and large civil contracts could provide a competitive advantage in the infrastructure and real estate sectors.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated EPC philosophy: "Generate positive cash flows from all the projects and re-invest to drive growth", with overall goal "Sustained growth driven by Execution Excellence & Financial Discipline".
- Net debt of Rs 152 Cr as on 30 June 2026 (Rs 151.74 Cr in the debt table) — up through the year from Rs 16.62 Cr at Mar-25, Rs 53.50 Cr at Sep-25 and Rs 91.41 Cr at Mar-26.
- Gross debt rose to Rs 338.76 Cr at Jun-26 from Rs 201.90 Cr at Mar-25, spread across banks (SBI/UBI/BOM/IndusInd/FDRL/KBL Rs 98.43 Cr) and NBFCs (Aditya Birla Capital Rs 82.48 Cr, Arka Fincap Rs 40.08 Cr, Vivriti Rs 39.87 Cr, SBM Bank Rs 24.00 Cr, Tata Capital Rs 21.01 Cr, ICICI Rs 13.01 Cr, Others Rs 19.88 Cr).
- Cash side at Jun-26: cash & bank Rs 31.86 Cr plus FD Rs 155.16 Cr for total cash & bank balance of Rs 187.02 Cr — but the deck footnotes "Lien FD - Rs 149.76 Crs", i.e. most of the FD is lien-marked.
- Credit lines: sanctioned Rs 760 Cr (fund-based Rs 112 Cr, non-fund-based Rs 648 Cr), utilised Rs 405 Cr, unutilised Rs 355 Cr, on "Strengthened relationships with financial institutions enabling higher sanctioned limits and timely resource mobilization".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Nearly four decades of engineering and construction experience, with a stated track record of 225+ projects and over 45 million sq. ft. delivered across multiple sectors
- Diversified dual-engine model across EPC and Real Estate Development that serves distinct market opportunities while sharing common execution capabilities
- Integrated in-house design, engineering and project execution capability spanning planning, procurement, construction and quality assurance
- Healthy order book with high government project participation, described as providing visibility of faster execution and uninterrupted cash flows
- Long-standing customer relationships and brand equity built on quality, reliability and timely execution
- Presence across 30+ locations in India, supporting a geographically diversified project pipeline
- Strategic execution partnership with the Adani Group, entered as a Memorandum of Understanding execution partner
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Project execution and timeline risk — Delays arising from labour shortages, adverse weather, approval bottlenecks or slower site mobilisation may impact project execution and revenue recognition; management states this remained a key challenge during FY26, particularly in the first half. Mitigation is robust project planning, improved site monitoring, disciplined resource allocation and a pipeline diversified across geographies.
- Margin pressure in the EPC business — Rising raw material costs, subcontractor inflation and execution inefficiencies may impact project profitability and operating margins, with fixed-price contracts further increasing cost sensitivity. Mitigation is better project selection, cost optimisation, strategic procurement and tighter contract structuring including escalation clauses where feasible.
- Real estate demand and sales risk — Slow inventory absorption, weaker consumer sentiment or elevated home loan interest rates may affect booking momentum and cash inflows from residential projects. Mitigation is a balanced portfolio across value housing, premium housing and redevelopment, with launches aligned to market demand and location attractiveness.
- Project and geographic concentration risk — Dependence on a few large projects or specific geographies may expose the business to localised disruptions or client-related risks. The disclosed EPC order book split is concentrated in Maharashtra at 52%, with Bihar 12%, Goa 9%, Tamil Nadu 9% and other 18%. Mitigation is continued diversification across EPC, real estate, redevelopment and strategic partnerships.
- End-market concentration in hospital / healthcare projects — The disclosed order book mix is heavily weighted to hospital projects at 52%, with residential 19%, institutional and others 16% and others 13%, leaving order inflow and execution exposed to the pace of public healthcare infrastructure awards.
- Regulatory and approval risk — Delays in statutory approvals, redevelopment clearances or regulatory changes may impact project launches and execution timelines. Mitigation is proactive regulatory engagement, strong compliance systems and early-stage due diligence.
- Competitive intensity — Increasing competition from regional and national players may exert pressure on bidding margins and market share. Mitigation cited is brand equity, nearly 40 years of execution experience, quality delivery and strategic partnerships such as the Adani collaboration.
- Macroeconomic, interest-rate and input-cost sensitivity — The Company states it is exposed to economic slowdown, fluctuations in raw material prices, project execution delays, labour shortages, regulatory changes and competitive pressures, and that changes in interest rates and delays in project approvals may also impact the construction and real estate sectors.

business.body: EPC Revenue: Rs 1,003.85 Cr; Real Estate Revenue: Rs 32.85 Cr
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Two segments presented side by side: Engineering Procurement & Construction ("One of the leading EPC Company in India") and Real Estate Development focused on mid-market residential in Mumbai & Pune.
- Track record markers: 45 Mn sq. ft. of projects delivered, 225+ projects delivered, 40 years of experience and presence across 30+ [locations] in India.
- EPC differentiation claimed through turnkey capability: "Higher margins Because of Turnkey Capabilities", an "In-house Design and Engineering team" and the "Ability to demand premium over other construction companies".
- Government orientation is the stated moat on cash flow: ~77% government projects, "Providing visibility of faster execution and uninterrupted Cash Flows", with the external EPC order book showing "Higher contribution by Government projects".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Approvals] Prakash CHS, Santacruz (W): "IOD & CC obtained; RERA registration underway"; Tower of Ascend has an application in process for Part-OC for G+3 with TDR loading for higher floors in progress.
- [Launch] Tranquil Heights, Powai was launched in the quarter — Phase 1 of 104 units (of 198 total), all sanctions including RERA received, shore-piling works underway, and the deck reports it is "Receiving a healthy response".
- [JV accounting] For Tranquil Heights (JV, 35% Vascon share) the deck footnotes: "Only the share of profit will be recognised in the books of accounts in accordance with Ind AS" — so its GDV does not flow through revenue.
- [Unbilled RE inventory] Across the five projects under development, area sold 0.52 msft of 0.70 msft attributable to Vascon, sale value Rs 396 Cr, collections Rs 280 Cr, revenue recognised Rs 127 Cr, balance revenue Rs 258 Cr and unsold inventory Rs 228 Cr.
- [Order discrepancy] The new CPWD order for the RBI Colony, Guwahati is stated as Rs 295 Cr on the highlights page but appears as "RBI Quarters, Guhawati / Assam / 293" in the order-book table; both readings are reproduced rather than reconciled.

business.body: Vascon Engineers conceives, develops, constructs and manages projects across residential, commercial, industrial, IT parks, hospitality, retail, education, healthcare and public infrastructure. Its EPC vertical delivers end-to-end, highly engineered turnkey construction for government agencies, institutions and reputed private clients, supported by in-house design and engineering capability, while its Real Estate vertical develops premium residential and mixed-use projects primarily in Pune and Mumbai through joint development and redevelopment structures. The Company states it has executed more than 225+ projects covering over 45 million sq. ft. across residential, commercial, institutional, industrial and infrastructure segments.

- **Real Estate Development:** Vascon ONYX, Santacruz, Mumbai

outlook.body: Total Order Book: Rs 2,717 Cr; External EPC Order Book: Rs 2,387 Cr; Government Project (%): 79%
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: The company has a strong pipeline of upcoming real estate projects, including Powai, Mumbai and Prakash Housing Society, which are expected to drive growth in the near term.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthening the EPC franchise - leveraging execution capability to expand the order book, deepen presence in government and institutional projects, and pursue large, high-value contracts that provide long-term revenue visibility
- Selective order acquisition in EPC alongside disciplined project execution, operational excellence and prudent financial management
- Accelerating project execution through disciplined project management, optimised resource deployment and timely completion, to improve profitability, cash flows and customer satisfaction
- Scaling the real estate portfolio by expediting completion of ongoing developments and advancing a pipeline of residential and commercial projects through an asset-light Joint Development (JD) / Joint Development Agreement (JDA) model
- Asset-light real estate growth via joint development and redevelopment opportunities in high-potential markets such as Mumbai and Pune, to improve capital efficiency and returns
- Driving financial discipline - maintaining a prudent capital structure by optimising debt, strengthening banking relationships, improving working capital efficiency and enhancing financial flexibility
- Building organisational excellence - investing in people, technology and governance to strengthen organisational capabilities and operational efficiency
- Investing in digital project monitoring, process automation and data-driven decision making to improve execution efficiency and strengthen governance
- Expanding into urban infrastructure and redevelopment through the partnership with Adani Infra (India) Limited, combining Vascon's execution capability with Adani's scale to pursue larger and more complex projects
- Commitment to responsible construction practices that minimise environmental impact
- Vascon frames capital allocation around capital efficiency rather than balance-sheet-heavy growth. The business model rests on disciplined capital allocation and prudent financial management, with an asset-light growth approach supported by strategic partnerships. In EPC, the stated policy is to maintain a strong focus on positive project cash flows, which the Company says enables reinvestment into capacity expansion, business growth and long-term value creation, alongside pursuing large, high-value contracts from government agencies and reputed private clients to improve order-book quality and visibility. In Real Estate, the Company leverages Joint Ventures and Joint Development Agreements with landowners to minimise upfront capital requirements and support scalable, capital-efficient expansion, supported by a lean operating model and a low cost base. No dividend policy, payout ratio or buyback intent is disclosed in this section.
- Innovation and sustainability is a stated strategy pillar: leverage technology and green practices to differentiate offerings, improve cost efficiency, and align with evolving customer and regulatory expectations
- Human capital: as of March 31, 2026 the Company had a total workforce of 751 employees with an annual attrition rate of 5%, and 401 employees underwent training during FY 2025-26 focused on technical capability building, leadership development and functional skill enhancement
- Employee well-being, workplace safety and inclusive growth are stated as key priorities, supported by engagement and welfare initiatives
- Internal control and governance: internal control systems commensurate with the scale of operations, with the internal audit function periodically reviewing operational, financial and compliance controls and observations reviewed by management and the Audit Committee
- Risk governance: risks are continuously evaluated through a structured risk management framework enabling timely mitigation
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Vascon does not describe a conventional plant-and-machinery capex programme; its expansion is footprint-, order-book- and partnership-led. On the EPC side, growth is being pursued through order book expansion - new orders from Royal Rides, Yucca Promoters, MSEB Holdings, Navi Mumbai and Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation took the order book to approximately Rs 2,717 crore (of which the external EPC order book is approximately Rs 2,387 crore and roughly 79% is government projects), while execution continues on marquee sites including Bihar Medical College, Capgemini IT Park and Pune Police Staff Quarters. The defining expansion step of the year was a Memorandum of Understanding with Adani Infra (India) Limited under which Vascon acts as an execution partner; management describes this as expanding its presence in the urban infrastructure and redevelopment segment and positioning it to pursue larger and more complex projects. In Real Estate, expansion is deliberately asset-light: management states it will grow through joint development and redevelopment opportunities in high-potential markets such as Mumbai and Pune, which it says enables efficient capital deployment, improves returns and supports sustainable expansion; ongoing developments include Vascon Goodlife, Tulip Phase III, Tower of Ascend and Orchids, with further real estate launches described as upcoming. The Company also continues to invest in digital project monitoring, process automation and data-driven decision making to improve execution efficiency. Its operating footprint comprises the registered office at Pune and major branch locations at Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh), Chennai, Mumbai, Panaji (Goa), Coimbatore and Ahmedabad. No rupee capital-expenditure budget, commissioning schedule or capacity-addition target is disclosed in this section.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management states that as it moves into FY27 the Company is well positioned to accelerate execution, capitalise on a healthy order book and deliver sustainable growth, with project execution conditions having gradually started normalising across key sites
- Government infrastructure-led growth: Union Budget 2026-27 capital expenditure increased to Rs 12.2 lakh crore covering roads, railways, metro networks, airports, energy and logistics
- ICRA expects India's construction sector to witness 6-8% revenue growth in FY27, compared with 2-4% growth in FY26, supported by improving order inflows and execution momentum
- India's construction market is expected to reach Rs 25.31 trillion in 2026 and to grow approximately 6.4% in real terms during 2026
- RBI projects India's real GDP to grow around 6.6% in FY27; the repo rate at 5.25% and stable to moderating home loan rates are expected to improve housing affordability and support residential demand
- Residential demand supported by urbanisation, rising household incomes and preference for home ownership; premium and redevelopment-led projects expected to be key growth drivers in major urban markets
- Premiumisation of residential demand - premium and luxury housing accounted for nearly 63% of total residential sales in 2025 versus 53% in 2024
- Commercial real estate momentum from GCC expansion, Grade-A office demand and flexible workspaces; office vacancy declined to 13.85% with gross leasing across top 8 cities at 21.9 million sq. ft.
- Industrial and warehousing expected to remain a high-growth segment, driven by manufacturing-led demand, logistics modernisation and institutional investment
- Infrastructure-led real estate growth and the rise of Tier-II and Tier-III cities are reshaping demand across micro-markets
- Institutionalisation and capital inflows - institutional investments in Indian real estate rose 23% YoY to USD 4.3 billion in H1 2026, with domestic capital at a record 64% share
- Government programmes (PM Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline, Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, PMAY) create a long-term pipeline of opportunities for construction and real estate companies
- IBEF projects India's real estate sector to reach US$ 5.8 trillion by 2047, contributing around 15.5% of GDP versus ~7.3% currently
- Management flags that FY26 saw temporary external challenges that impacted the pace of execution, offset by focus on execution discipline, productivity improvement and cost control
- Management states new orders from Royal Rides, Yucca Promoters, MSEB Holdings, Navi Mumbai and Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation further strengthened the order book to approximately Rs 2,717 crore, providing healthy revenue visibility
- The EPC business remained the principal contributor to performance and maintained healthy execution across marquee projects including Bihar Medical College, Capgemini IT Park and Pune Police Staff Quarters
- Management cites a healthy order book, robust project pipeline and upcoming real estate launches as sources of confidence for sustainable and profitable growth
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Vascon Engineers Ltd is a leading EPC company in India with a strong presence in the infrastructure and real estate sectors, focusing on mid-market residential projects and large civil contracts. The company has a healthy order book and is poised for growth with a robust working capital position and strengthened relationships with financial institutions. However, the company faces risks such as cash flow constraints and internal organizational changes.

open.item: Management states that as it moves into FY27 the Company is well positioned to accelerate execution, capitalise on a healthy order book and deliver sustainable growth.

The Company will expand into the urban infrastructure and redevelopment segment through its partnership with Adani Infra (India) Limited, combining Vascon's execution capabilities with Adani's scale to pursue larger and more complex projects.

The Company will continue to strengthen its EPC business through selective order acquisition, disciplined project execution, operational excellence and prudent financial management, deepening presence in government and institutional projects.
In Real Estate the Company will pursue an asset-light growth strategy through joint development and redevelopment opportunities in high-potential markets such as Mumbai and Pune.

The Company intends to maintain a prudent capital structure by optimising debt, strengthening banking relationships, improving working capital efficiency and enhancing financial flexibility to support future growth.
The Company will continue to invest in digital project monitoring, process automation and data-driven decision making to improve execution efficiency and strengthen governance.

The Company will expand into urban infrastructure and redevelopment through its Memorandum of Understanding with Adani Infra (India) Limited as an execution partner, positioning it to pursue larger and more complex projects.

Real estate expansion will be pursued on an asset-light basis through joint development and redevelopment in Mumbai and Pune, which management says enables efficient capital deployment and supports sustainable expansion.

Management points to upcoming real estate launches and a robust project pipeline as a source of forward growth, alongside ongoing developments such as Vascon Goodlife, Tulip Phase III, Tower of Ascend and Orchids; no launch dates or areas are quantified in this section.
The Company will continue investing in digital project monitoring, process automation and data-driven decision making to improve execution efficiency and strengthen governance.

The defining expansion step of the year was a Memorandum of Understanding with Adani Infra (India) Limited under which Vascon acts as an execution partner; management describes this as expanding its presence in the urban infrastructure and redevelopment segment and positioning it to pursue larger and more complex projects. Its operating footprint comprises the registered office at Pune and major branch locations at Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh), Chennai, Mumbai, Panaji (Goa), Coimbatore and Ahmedabad. No rupee capital-expenditure budget, commissioning schedule or capacity-addition target is disclosed in this section.

risks.note: Delays arising from labour shortages, adverse weather, approval bottlenecks or slower site mobilisation may impact project execution and revenue recognition; management states this remained a key challenge during FY26, particularly in the first half. Mitigation is robust project planning, improved site monitoring, disciplined resource allocation and a pipeline diversified across geographies.

risks.risk: Margin pressure in the EPC business
risks.note: Rising raw material costs, subcontractor inflation and execution inefficiencies may impact project profitability and operating margins, with fixed-price contracts further increasing cost sensitivity. Mitigation is better project selection, cost optimisation, strategic procurement and tighter contract structuring including escalation clauses where feasible.

risks.risk: Real estate demand and sales risk
risks.note: Slow inventory absorption, weaker consumer sentiment or elevated home loan interest rates may affect booking momentum and cash inflows from residential projects. Mitigation is a balanced portfolio across value housing, premium housing and redevelopment, with launches aligned to market demand and location attractiveness.

Dependence on a few large projects or specific geographies may expose the business to localised disruptions or client-related risks. The disclosed EPC order book split is concentrated in Maharashtra at 52%, with Bihar 12%, Goa 9%, Tamil Nadu 9% and other 18%. Mitigation is continued diversification across EPC, real estate, redevelopment and strategic partnerships.

risks.risk: End-market concentration in hospital / healthcare projects
risks.note: The disclosed order book mix is heavily weighted to hospital projects at 52%, with residential 19%, institutional and others 16% and others 13%, leaving order inflow and execution exposed to the pace of public healthcare infrastructure awards.

Delays in statutory approvals, redevelopment clearances or regulatory changes may impact project launches and execution timelines. Mitigation is proactive regulatory engagement, strong compliance systems and early-stage due diligence.

Increasing competition from regional and national players may exert pressure on bidding margins and market share. Mitigation cited is brand equity, nearly 40 years of execution experience, quality delivery and strategic partnerships such as the Adani collaboration.

The Company states it is exposed to economic slowdown, fluctuations in raw material prices, project execution delays, labour shortages, regulatory changes and competitive pressures, and that changes in interest rates and delays in project approvals may also impact the construction and real estate sectors.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Founded in 1986 and now in its fifth decade, Vascon Engineers is an India-focused engineering, construction and real estate company operating two complementary verticals - EPC contracting (increasingly government and institutional) and asset-light real estate development in Pune and Mumbai.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Vascon Engineers conceives, develops, constructs and manages projects across residential, commercial, industrial, IT parks, hospitality, retail, education, healthcare and public infrastructure. Its EPC vertical delivers end-to-end, highly engineered turnkey construction for government agencies, institutions and reputed private clients, supported by in-house design and engineering capability, while its Real Estate vertical develops premium residential and mixed-use projects primarily in Pune and Mumbai through joint development and redevelopment structures. The Company states it has executed more than 225+ projects covering over 45 million sq. ft. across residential, commercial, institutional, industrial and infrastructure segments.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management states that as it moves into FY27 the Company is well positioned to accelerate execution, capitalise on a healthy order book and deliver sustainable growth, with project execution conditions having gradually started normalising across key sites
- Government infrastructure-led growth: Union Budget 2026-27 capital expenditure increased to Rs 12.2 lakh crore covering roads, railways, metro networks, airports, energy and logistics
- ICRA expects India's construction sector to witness 6-8% revenue growth in FY27, compared with 2-4% growth in FY26, supported by improving order inflows and execution momentum
- India's construction market is expected to reach Rs 25.31 trillion in 2026 and to grow approximately 6.4% in real terms during 2026
- RBI projects India's real GDP to grow around 6.6% in FY27; the repo rate at 5.25% and stable to moderating home loan rates are expected to improve housing affordability and support residential demand
- Residential demand supported by urbanisation, rising household incomes and preference for home ownership; premium and redevelopment-led projects expected to be key growth drivers in major urban markets
- Premiumisation of residential demand - premium and luxury housing accounted for nearly 63% of total residential sales in 2025 versus 53% in 2024
- Commercial real estate momentum from GCC expansion, Grade-A office demand and flexible workspaces; office vacancy declined to 13.85% with gross leasing across top 8 cities at 21.9 million sq. ft.
- Industrial and warehousing expected to remain a high-growth segment, driven by manufacturing-led demand, logistics modernisation and institutional investment
- Infrastructure-led real estate growth and the rise of Tier-II and Tier-III cities are reshaping demand across micro-markets
- Institutionalisation and capital inflows - institutional investments in Indian real estate rose 23% YoY to USD 4.3 billion in H1 2026, with domestic capital at a record 64% share
- Government programmes (PM Gati Shakti, National Infrastructure Pipeline, Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, PMAY) create a long-term pipeline of opportunities for construction and real estate companies
- IBEF projects India's real estate sector to reach US$ 5.8 trillion by 2047, contributing around 15.5% of GDP versus ~7.3% currently
- Management flags that FY26 saw temporary external challenges that impacted the pace of execution, offset by focus on execution discipline, productivity improvement and cost control
- Management states new orders from Royal Rides, Yucca Promoters, MSEB Holdings, Navi Mumbai and Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation further strengthened the order book to approximately Rs 2,717 crore, providing healthy revenue visibility
- The EPC business remained the principal contributor to performance and maintained healthy execution across marquee projects including Bihar Medical College, Capgemini IT Park and Pune Police Staff Quarters
- Management cites a healthy order book, robust project pipeline and upcoming real estate launches as sources of confidence for sustainable and profitable growth

capex_expansion.body: Vascon does not describe a conventional plant-and-machinery capex programme; its expansion is footprint-, order-book- and partnership-led. On the EPC side, growth is being pursued through order book expansion - new orders from Royal Rides, Yucca Promoters, MSEB Holdings, Navi Mumbai and Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation took the order book to approximately Rs 2,717 crore (of which the external EPC order book is approximately Rs 2,387 crore and roughly 79% is government projects), while execution continues on marquee sites including Bihar Medical College, Capgemini IT Park and Pune Police Staff Quarters. The defining expansion step of the year was a Memorandum of Understanding with Adani Infra (India) Limited under which Vascon acts as an execution partner; management describes this as expanding its presence in the urban infrastructure and redevelopment segment and positioning it to pursue larger and more complex projects. In Real Estate, expansion is deliberately asset-light: management states it will grow through joint development and redevelopment opportunities in high-potential markets such as Mumbai and Pune, which it says enables efficient capital deployment, improves returns and supports sustainable expansion; ongoing developments include Vascon Goodlife, Tulip Phase III, Tower of Ascend and Orchids, with further real estate launches described as upcoming. The Company also continues to invest in digital project monitoring, process automation and data-driven decision making to improve execution efficiency. Its operating footprint comprises the registered office at Pune and major branch locations at Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh), Chennai, Mumbai, Panaji (Goa), Coimbatore and Ahmedabad. No rupee capital-expenditure budget, commissioning schedule or capacity-addition target is disclosed in this section.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Approvals] Prakash CHS, Santacruz (W): "IOD & CC obtained; RERA registration underway"; Tower of Ascend has an application in process for Part-OC for G+3 with TDR loading for higher floors in progress.
- [Launch] Tranquil Heights, Powai was launched in the quarter — Phase 1 of 104 units (of 198 total), all sanctions including RERA received, shore-piling works underway, and the deck reports it is "Receiving a healthy response".
- [JV accounting] For Tranquil Heights (JV, 35% Vascon share) the deck footnotes: "Only the share of profit will be recognised in the books of accounts in accordance with Ind AS" — so its GDV does not flow through revenue.
- [Unbilled RE inventory] Across the five projects under development, area sold 0.52 msft of 0.70 msft attributable to Vascon, sale value Rs 396 Cr, collections Rs 280 Cr, revenue recognised Rs 127 Cr, balance revenue Rs 258 Cr and unsold inventory Rs 228 Cr.
- [Order discrepancy] The new CPWD order for the RBI Colony, Guwahati is stated as Rs 295 Cr on the highlights page but appears as "RBI Quarters, Guhawati / Assam / 293" in the order-book table; both readings are reproduced rather than reconciled.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
